title: Outcome of a GitLab connection write or check
description: outcome: written (glab's file now holds the change), unchanged (it already did; a repeated request after a lost reply is observed, not replayed), absent (the entry to log out held no token already) or checked. api is GitLab's answer for this token now, given only by connect, replace and check; it is never Git readiness, which connection.git observes separately. token is what GitLab says about the token now, given with api ok. A missing write_repository is no refusal: the connection is made and token.push says no. A connect whose helper registration failed still answers with the connection and its git state, so the page offers repair rather than a working connection. Refusals are fixed error codes in the error shape: nothing was written.

api.description: token_expired is GitLab's own 'Token is expired'; token_rejected any other 401 (revoked, mistyped, another server's). insufficient_scope means the token cannot read the API (read_api is missing). not_gitlab: the address answered something other than GitLab's API.

token.description: GET /personal_access_tokens/self as GitLab answered it now; nothing stores it. push: yes when the scopes include write_repository or api, no when GitLab lists the scopes and neither is there, unknown when GitLab did not describe the token (fine-grained, group or project tokens on some servers, older GitLab) or it is fine-grained, whose push the scopes do not tell. scopes, expires_at (null: no expiry) and fine are present only when GitLab described the token.
